claims.text: SelfCheckGPT with Prompt achieves an AUC-PR score of 93.42 in sentence-level non-factual hallucination detection on GPT-3 generated WikiBio passages.
SelfCheckGPT with Prompt achieves an AUC-PR score of 53.19 in detecting major-inaccurate (non-factual*) sentences in non-total hallucination passages.
SelfCheckGPT with Prompt achieves a Pearson correlation score of 78.32 with human judgments in passage-level factuality assessment.
SelfCheckGPT with NLI achieves an AUC-PR score of 92.50 in sentence-level non-factual hallucination detection on GPT-3 generated WikiBio passages.
SelfCheckGPT detects hallucinations in black-box generative large language models in a zero-resource manner without requiring external databases or output token probabilities.
Output token average log probability from the generating LLM achieves an AUC-PR score of 83.21 in sentence-level non-factual hallucination detection.

evidence.description: Table 2 reports an AUC-PR of 93.42 for SelfCheckGPT w/ Prompt on NonFact sentence-level hallucination detection compared to the random baseline of 72.96.
Table 2 reports an AUC-PR of 53.19 for SelfCheckGPT w/ Prompt on NonFact* sentence-level detection compared to the random baseline of 29.72.
Table 2 lists a Pearson correlation of 78.32 and Spearman rank correlation of 78.30 for SelfCheckGPT w/ Prompt against human factuality annotations at the passage level.
Table 2 shows SelfCheckGPT w/ NLI obtaining an AUC-PR of 92.50 for sentence-level NonFact detection and 74.14 Pearson correlation at the passage level.

Section 5 describes SelfCheckGPT generating stochastically sampled responses using the same prompt to assess informational consistency without external database retrieval or probability distributions.
Table 2 lists GPT-3 Avg(-log p) achieving 83.21 AUC-PR on NonFact sentence-level hallucination detection.

methodologies.name: SelfCheckGPT
methodologies.description: A sampling-based zero-resource hallucination detection framework that measures consistency between a target LLM output and multiple stochastically sampled outputs from the same prompt.

limitations.text: Evaluation dataset was limited to 238 GPT-3 generated passages predominantly focusing on individuals from the WikiBio dataset.
Factuality evaluation is performed at sentence level, whereas a single sentence can contain a mixture of factual and non-factual atomic claims.
SelfCheckGPT with Prompt incur high inference computational costs due to multiple LLM evaluation calls per sentence.
Grey-box factuality assessment methods require token-level output probability distributions, which are often unavailable in commercial API-based LLMs like ChatGPT.
Fact-verification approaches require external databases that can be complex to interface and are limited to knowledge present in the database.

future_work.text: Extend hallucination detection evaluations to broader domains beyond biography passages, such as locations and objects.
Decompose generated sentences into sub-sentence atomic facts for fine-grained factuality evaluation.
Improve the efficiency and reduce computational costs of prompt-based SelfCheckGPT methods.
